subject: general
question: Which Article establishes the office of the President?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 52**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 52** of the Indian Constitution establishes the office of the President of India.
 
• The President is the **head of state** and the highest constitutional authority in India.
 
• The article specifically mentions that India shall have a President, ensuring a parliamentary system of governance under the Constitution.
 
• The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The President holds office for a tenure of **five years** and serves as the formal head of the executive, legislative, and judiciary branches, as well as the commander-in-chief of the Indian Armed Forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 75**

 
 
• Article 75 deals with the appointment of the Prime Minister and other Ministers by the President.
 
• It states that the President shall appoint the Prime Minister, and the other Ministers shall be appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• It also mentions that the Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.
 
• The article further provides that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Article 53**
 
 
• Article 53 states that the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President.
 
• The President exercises this power either directly or through officers subordinate to him, in accordance with the Constitution.
 
• This article establishes the President as the formal executive authority while the real powers are exercised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Article 74**
 
 
• Article 74 defines the role of the Council of Ministers in aiding and advising the President.
 
• It states that there shall be a Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President in the exercise of his functions.
 
• The President is bound to act according to the advice given by the Council of Ministers.
 
• This article ensures the functioning of the parliamentary form of government in India.
